title: 05 · Weaver — same request, two verdicts
description: Governance. Weaver publishes no telemetry of its own — its verdict goes to its container log. These panels are the traces it is judging.

options.content:
### Weaver live-check
Weaver's verdict prints to its container log — run `docker compose logs weaver-livecheck`. This dashboard shows the two trace streams it is judging, side by side.

**Open one trace from each table and compare the attribute names.** Same HTTP request, same registry, two different verdicts.

panels.description: How to read Weaver's verdict, and which container log it prints to.

panels.title: Demo 1 — pinned to semconv v1.26.0 → VIOLATIONS
panels.description: Demo 1's traces — the input Weaver rejects. http.method is deprecated and http.path is not in the registry.

panels.title: Demo 2 — current conventions → CLEAN
panels.description: Demo 2's traces — the input Weaver accepts. Nobody tried harder; they just never typed the names.

options.content:
### What Weaver flags
```
Span handle_request `internal`
    http.method = GET
        - [violation] deprecated; renamed to `http.request.method`
    http.path = /hello
        - [violation] does not exist in the registry
```
Checked against the **live upstream registry**, pulled from GitHub at startup — so a rename in the next OTel release is flagged the same day.
